takeaway: Parietal cells make intrinsic factor, which binds vitamin B12 for absorption in the ileum. After total gastrectomy they are absent, so B12 must be injected for life.

question.text: Before a total gastrectomy he is told he needs lifelong B12 injections. Absence of which cell type is responsible?

lines.text: A total gastrectomy removes the whole stomach.
And with it go the parietal cells.
Intrinsic factor binds vitamin B twelve in the stomach, so it can be absorbed in the ileum.
lines.say: Intrinsic factor binds vitamin B twelve in the stomach, so it can be absorbed in the ileum. (sigh)

lines.text: Without it, the capsule has no key, and the ileum gate stays locked.
So the patient needs lifelong injections.
G cells make gastrin, and goblet cells live in the bowel, so they are not the answer.
